source_snapshot.test_name_items: NonSecure Create LDAP Configuration by openbmctool
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1.Download the opembmc-tools on Git-hub : https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc-tools/tree/master/
2.Install openbmc tool
2. Send command : ./openbmctool  -H $BMCIP -U root -P 0penBmc ldap enable --uri="ldap://<ldap server IP/hostname>" --bindDN=<bindDN> --baseDN=<basDN> --bindPassword=<bindPassword> --scope="sub/one/base" --serverType="OpenLDAP/ActiveDirectory"
Note:
-- configuring FQDN (fully qualified domain name/ hostname) in the "uri" parameter requires that DNS server be configured on the BMC.
-- Currently, openbmctool doesn't support configuring the DNS server on the BMC.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Command should be sent successfully
2.certificate should be upload seccessfully.
Note:
-- configuring FQDN (fully qualified domain name/ hostname) in the "uri" parameter requires that DNS server be configured on the BMC.
-- Currently, openbmctool doesn't support configuring the DNS server on the BMC.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: openbmctool.py (openbmc-tools, install) + reachable LDAP server URI
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- NonSecure Create LDAP Configuration by openbmctool (NonSecure LDAP config): `openbmctool ${BMC_CONN:?operator must supply openbmctool target, e.g. http://${BMC_USER}:${BMC_PASS}@${BMC_IP}:8080/} ldap enable --uri="ldap://${LDAP_SERVER:?operator must supply the LDAP server FQDN/IP}"` (openbmctool from openbmc-tools, user supplies the LDAP server / FQDN). Agent runs it and verifies command success + cert upload.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the openbmctool command output + HTTP 200 so the user confirms the NonSecure LDAP config applied; certificate uploaded successfully.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: enabling LDAP on the BMC changes auth/policy; use the intended LDAP server and confirm the URI/FQDN.

original_test_intent: Verify openbmctool can create the intended non-secure `ldap://` BMC LDAP configuration with the selected URI, bind/base DN, search scope and server type, and that the resulting external-authentication behavior works without losing local administrative recovery.
original_method: In an explicitly approved isolated lab, pin and review openbmctool, preserve the current BMC auth configuration and independent local recovery, validate BMC-to-LDAP DNS or IP connectivity, apply the complete cleartext LDAP configuration once using protected secret injection, read back the redacted state, prove allowed and denied LDAP authentication plus role mapping and local fallback, then disable or restore the baseline.
manual_activity: A security owner approves the cleartext-LDAP exception and isolated topology, selects LDAP parameters/roles/test identities and safeguards secrets. A human retains an independent local-admin session and recovery path, verifies authentication behavior and restores the configuration. Automation may run the pinned tool and collect redacted state only after point-of-action approval.
required_inputs: BMC/firmware identity and supported openbmctool API/version
Approved isolated network and non-secure LDAP security exception
LDAP/AD server IP or resolvable FQDN, port, bind DN, base DN, scope and serverType
Protected bind/BMC/test-account secrets and rotation plan
Expected test user/group/role, denied identity and local-admin fallback matrix
Current auth/LDAP/policy export and independent console/local recovery
Disable/restore method and bounded authentication validation window
Engineer disposition of the copied certificate-upload Criterion
safety_requirements: Do not use the literal `root`/`0penBmc`, place BMC or bind passwords in command lines, URLs, shell history, process listings, logs, screenshots or review records.
Permit `ldap://` only in an approved isolated non-production network; cleartext LDAP must not cross an untrusted management path.
Do not clear BMC or security audit logs. Preserve the original auth policy and verify an independent local-admin/console recovery path before enabling external authentication.
Obtain point-of-action approval for one full configuration write; because openbmctool recreates the object for property changes, do not experiment or retry with partial parameters.
Do not treat HTTP 200 or command acceptance as authentication success, and do not claim CA-certificate upload from this non-secure command.
Stop on target/endpoint mismatch, exposed secrets, unexpected role mapping, local fallback failure, lockout, inability to disable/restore or unexplained certificate behavior.
agent_execution_scope: Validate the isolated topology, tool provenance, target, full LDAP semantics, DNS/connectivity, protected secrets, auth matrix, current state and recovery; present the exact redacted action for approval.
After approval, apply one complete non-secure LDAP configuration with protected secret injection and capture redacted tool/API/audit and configuration readback.
Test the dedicated allowed LDAP identity, denied identity, group/role mapping and independent local-admin fallback without clearing logs.
Disable or restore the approved baseline, confirm access, archive redacted evidence and stop without certificate claim, automatic retry or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve cleartext LDAP only for the isolated lab and approve the pinned tool, endpoint, complete parameters, auth matrix and protected secret handling.
Resolve whether the certificate-upload Criterion is erroneous copied text or a separate secure-LDAP checkpoint.
Approve the one-time configuration, recovery/restore and acceptance; review auth and audit evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It omits bindDN, baseDN, bindPassword, scope and serverType that define the source operation, puts credentials in a URL-shaped variable, and cannot prove certificate upload or LDAP authentication from HTTP 200. The source command itself also embeds unsafe default-looking credentials and a command-line bind secret.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain the pinned vendor openbmctool `ldap enable` path and all source LDAP fields, but pass BMC/bind secrets only through a reviewed protected mechanism supported by the approved tool; target one verified isolated BMC and do not invent certificate upload.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The openbmctool download/install requirement, `ldap://` URI, bind/base DN, sub/one/base scope, OpenLDAP/ActiveDirectory choice, FQDN/DNS caveat, source command/credentials, Criteria conflict, no Script and 10/0-minute estimates remain preserved as evidence rather than silently corrected.

modernized_recommendation.status: PROJECT EXECUTION READINESS PENDING; ENGINEER DECISION PENDING FOR CRITERIA CONFLICT
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a reviewed pinned openbmctool in an isolated lab with protected secrets, full parameter readback, positive/negative LDAP login, role mapping, local fallback and deterministic disable/restore.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected OpenBMC implementation and its supported LDAP configuration API against the approved lab LDAP/AD service.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC firmware/API, openbmctool commit/runtime and LDAP/AD server versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Pinned openbmc-tools documentation/source, vendor BMC LDAP schema, Project authentication/security policy and recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Eliminates literal/default credentials and command-line secret exposure, verifies authentication rather than command acceptance, and separates unsupported certificate wording while retaining non-secure LDAP semantics.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A vendor API override must document uncovered openbmctool coverage; secure LDAPS/CA trust belongs to the next case; command success is not login/role/fallback coverage.

modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Cleartext LDAP exposes credentials and alters BMC authentication; DNS or scope errors can cause lockout; recreating the object can replace existing settings.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use a supported vendor API or WebUI only when it records the original openbmctool path, actual method, reason, engineer approval, field/auth equivalence and unverified tool coverage. It may not reinterpret this row as secure LDAPS or CA-certificate installation.
expected_evidence: Security exception/isolation, verified BMC/firmware, pinned tool commit/runtime, LDAP server/network/DNS facts and redacted pre-change auth/LDAP/policy state
Approved URI/port/bind/base/scope/serverType and protected-secret handling record without any credential values
One redacted openbmctool/API response, audit entry and independent configuration readback showing the exact intended non-secure object
Allowed LDAP login, denied login, group/role mapping and separate local-admin fallback evidence tied to the configured endpoint
Disable/restore and post-access proof, preserved logs/secret rotation as applicable, unresolved certificate criterion disposition and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title and Procedure create a non-secure `ldap://` configuration and contain no certificate upload step, while Criteria 2 requires a certificate to upload successfully. That checkpoint aligns more naturally with the following secure `ldaps://` case and cannot be claimed from this command. Master remains preserved; an engineer must decide whether the criterion is copied text or a separately required action.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The non-secure LDAP configuration and authentication purpose is identifiable despite the conflicting certificate line. Execution can remain readiness/decision pending while the cleartext exception, complete parameters, safe secret path and recovery are supplied; the conflict does not justify inventing coverage or a permanent BLOCKED status.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE but restores every source LDAP field, removes credential-bearing shorthand, requires isolated approval and real authentication/rollback evidence, and flags certificate upload as unsupported.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with its security controls and explicitly records the Master Criteria inconsistency as a source conflict requiring engineer ownership.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces a command/HTTP-only gate with complete LDAP state and positive/negative/role/local-recovery verification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Keeps secure LDAPS and CA trust in the next row; their evidence cannot satisfy this cleartext configuration row.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents exposed credentials, auth lockout and a false certificate-upload claim while preserving the source's distinct non-secure openbmctool coverage and assigning the contradictory criterion to an engineer.
independent_technical_reasoning: LDAP configuration success is meaningful only if the BMC resolves/reaches the intended directory, stores the exact search semantics, maps the approved identity correctly, rejects an invalid identity and retains local recovery. `ldap://` provides no transport confidentiality, so its use needs an isolated exception. The command has no CA object or upload action, making Criteria 2 impossible to prove without adding an unrelated operation; that is a source conflict, not permission to silently rewrite Master.
